name: fd
summary: A Rust filesystem finder that combines regex or glob matching, ignore-aware parallel traversal, metadata predicates, and parallel per-entry or batched command execution.

features.name: Ignore-aware parallel filesystem walk
features.description: The official README describes parallelized directory traversal with hidden and Git-ignored entries excluded by default. The fixed walk implementation configures ignore sources, overrides, thread count, and a parallel walker.
benefits: Reduces traversal time for large directory trees
Provides useful project-oriented defaults while retaining explicit unrestricted modes
costs: Default exclusions can hide entries unless users understand the policy
Concurrent traversal requires coordination of errors, cancellation, and result delivery

features.name: Composable path and metadata filters
features.description: fd accepts regex or glob patterns and composes path, type, extension, depth, size, owner, time, exclusion, and ignore-contain constraints. The fixed source applies these predicates while consuming walker entries.
benefits: Expresses common filesystem queries without shelling out to multiple tools
Allows traversal results to be narrowed before output or execution
costs: Predicate interactions make matching semantics less obvious than a single pattern
Metadata checks can add filesystem calls and platform-specific behavior

features.name: Parallel command execution boundary
features.description: The official documentation distinguishes per-result execution from one batched command and states that per-result jobs can run in parallel. The fixed source distributes jobs across worker threads and buffers or streams their output.
benefits: Turns a filesystem query into a bounded batch or parallel job fan-out
Keeps output from concurrent commands from being interlaced
costs: External command failure, side effects, and ordering become part of the invocation contract
Parallelism can amplify resource consumption and expose filesystem races

mathematical_views.question: How do pattern, path, metadata, ignore, and exclusion predicates select entries from a filesystem walk?
assumptions: A walker emits entries and each option contributes a predicate or traversal constraint
Predicates are composed as conjunctions except where an option explicitly changes traversal or matching mode
The model abstracts symlink races, permission failures, and platform metadata differences

mathematical_views.question: How do discovered entries become serialized output, per-entry jobs, or a single batch command under bounded parallelism?
assumptions: Entries move through discovered, filtered, queued, executed, and reported states
Worker count bounds concurrent job execution but does not make external commands deterministic
The view abstracts shell argument escaping details and process scheduling

benefits: Fast project-oriented traversal with configurable exclusions
costs: Concurrent traversal and implicit ignore policy affect completeness and ordering

benefits: Rich filesystem selection in one CLI boundary
costs: Predicate composition and metadata access increase semantic complexity

benefits: Search results can drive parallel or batched workflows
costs: External side effects and resource contention are delegated to the caller
